payload.title: Ward Twenty
payload.blurb: Tokyo, present day. Ghouls live in the city among humans, and most people never learn that the quiet student beside them on the train eats people to stay alive. You are a student in the 20th Ward, with a part-time job and a flat near the station. The Commission of Counter Ghoul has started walking…
payload.overview: Tokyo, present day: a city of rail lines, convenience stores and crowded streets in which ghouls live among humans. A ghoul looks human, talks like a neighbor and must eat human flesh to stay alive. Most ghouls pass for ordinary workers, students and shopkeepers, and their hunger is kept in check by careful habits and careful feeding. The Commission of Counter Ghoul, the CCG, hunts them with quinque weapons forged from the kagune of dead ghouls, and it runs district offices, blood checks and patrols in every ward. Each ward has its own feel. The 20th Ward is quiet: narrow lanes, old houses, a university on the western hill and a coffee shop called Anteiku. The 11th Ward next door is where crews of ghouls stop hiding as carefully and where the CCG rarely goes without a squad. There are no levels, classes or status windows here. Humans and ghouls share the city under an unwritten peace: ghouls do not feed inside the ward, humans do not hunt the ghouls who keep the peace, and both sides look away. The peace holds only while the rule holds.
payload.intro: The sign on the door of Anteiku still reads CLOSED, though the lamps inside have been lit since six. The lane outside is narrow and wet from the night rain, and the only sound is the coffee machine cooling behind the counter. Yoshimura stands at the bar with a folded towel on his shoulder, as unhurried as the clock above him. You are standing outside with your bag on your shoulder. At the back table Touka Kirishima has a stack of chemistry notes squared against the wood, unopened. Across the lane a CCG van has sat with its engine off since before dawn. The newspaper on the counter is folded to a column about a body found in the 17th Ward, drained and left under a bridge. The bell over the door has not rung yet today, and the door is unlocked.
starters: The bookshop on the main road closes at nine, and by eight the only customer is Hideyoshi Nagachika, who everyone calls Hide, reading the back of a paperback he has no plan to buy. Rain runs down the awning outside. Taped inside the door is a printed notice from the Commission of Counter Ghoul, a neat sheet asking shopkeepers to report anyone absent for more than a week, with a phone line and a case number in bold. Hide has a matching sheet folded in his denim jacket, and the look of someone who found something funny a minute ago and stopped finding it funny. Across the road a man in a navy suit has been standing under the streetlamp for twenty minutes without lighting the cigarette in his hand. Hide unfolds his sheet and holds it up beside the one on the door, so you can read both case numbers, and waits for you to say you have seen the number before.

The laundromat on the side street behind Kamii Station has one television bolted high in the corner, the evening news playing with the sound too low to follow. Chieko Hara has run this place for twenty years. Her blue apron has a pen clipped to the pocket, and a shoebox of unclaimed socks sits on the shelf by the door with a handwritten sign that says take what you need. Four dryers turn behind the glass, and their hum shakes the floor a little. On the screen a reporter stands before police tape in the 11th Ward and says the words Binge Eater without smiling. Plastic chairs face the window, all empty but one. Your load is in the third dryer with about fifteen minutes left, and the man in the last chair has not looked up from his phone once since you came in. Chieko wipes her hands on her apron and says, 'You ride the number 14 home, don't you? Sit a minute. The woman on the news just named the stops.'
starterTitles: The bookshop on the main road

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 19, a second-year at Kamii University in the 20th Ward. You live alone in a small flat a short walk from the station, work two evenings a week at a bookshop on the main road, and know a few faces from your seminars but nobody well. You are an ordinary person with an ordinary life, and nobody has looked at you twice yet.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
Commission of Counter Ghoul - The state agency that hunts ghouls, wants the city quiet, and reads every missing-person report as a possible ghoul case.
Anteiku - The coffee shop and back room that keep a few ghouls fed and alive, and want the peace held until the Binge Eater is stopped.
The 11th Ward crews - Ghoul gangs in the dangerous ward next door, who want the 20th Ward's quiet broken so their own trade can move in.
Kamii welfare circle - Welfare workers and a few professors who keep the missing-person files and want the names read aloud before the police close them.

entries.title: The world in one breath
entries.content: Tokyo looks like any city of glass and rail, but a small share of its people are ghouls: human-shaped predators who must eat human flesh to live. Ghouls mostly live quietly among humans, and most people never know who sat beside them on the train. The Commission of Counter Ghoul hunts them, and most citizens want it to keep doing so.

entries.title: RC cells, the rule under everything
entries.content: Every person carries RC cells in the blood. In humans they are inert. In ghouls they are numerous and active: they grow kagune, the organs that come out of the spine or back, and they are what makes a ghoul need human flesh. Feeding raises a ghoul's RC count, and a count that runs too high draws the Commission's attention.

entries.title: The 20th Ward
entries.content: The 20th Ward is a quiet residential ward on the north edge of central Tokyo, with narrow lanes of two-storey houses, small shrines and a station on the main line where the morning crowds go south to the offices. Most of its people have lived here for decades. Kamii University sits on its western hill. Residents like to keep it calm, and the CCG is seen here less than in other wards.

entries.title: Anteiku
entries.content: Anteiku is a coffee shop at the end of a narrow lane off the main street, with a bell over the door, dark wood and a back room that few customers see. Yoshimura runs it, and Touka Kirishima works there part time. Humans and ghouls both drink coffee there. The back room is where a ghoul who has not eaten can be fed without a single living person being harmed. Few people know that, and fewer say it aloud.

entries.title: Kamii University
entries.content: Kamii University is a mid-sized private university on the western hill of the 20th Ward. Its faculties run from economics and pharmacy to sociology and art. Students take the bus or walk up from the station, and the campus gate has a guard booth that the CCG now visits each morning. The notice boards carry the best gossip in the ward.

entries.title: Names in the ward
entries.content: Names are Japanese, written here with the given name first, as in Touka Kirishima. Families in the ward are Mizuno, Sugita, Tomita and Yamane. Given names run old to new: Chieko and Tatsuya for the old, Shinji, Kaoru, Natsumi and Eita for the young. Places are named for what the ward grew around: Kamii Station, the western hill, the main road.

entries.title: Ghouls
entries.content: A ghoul looks human and can pass as human for years. To live, a ghoul must eat human flesh. Other food can be eaten, but it gives a ghoul no strength. A ghoul who goes too long without flesh grows weak, then starts to hunt. Fed ghouls have sharp senses, quick healing and great strength. Most ghouls are careful. Some are not.

entries.title: Kagune
entries.content: A kagune is a ghoul's organ, grown from RC cells and drawn out of the spine or back when the ghoul fights or feeds. Three kinds are common. Rinkaku are many-tendrilled and whip quick. Koukaku form armored plates that take a blow. Ukaku are bladed, wing-shaped and cut as they open. Each ghoul's kagune suits its body and its hunting.

entries.title: The Commission of Counter Ghoul
entries.content: The Commission of Counter Ghoul, the CCG, is the government agency that hunts ghouls. Its investigators are ranked by class and work from district offices, and its squads carry out raids, blood checks and campus sweeps. It keeps files on known ghouls and presents a clean, polite face to the public. It believes it protects the city. Its critics say it kills first and records later.

entries.title: Quinque
entries.content: Quinque are weapons the CCG forges from the kagune of dead ghouls. Each is shaped to the ghoul it came from, and only a person whose RC cells can take hold of it can use it properly. Investigators carry them as scythes, blades or long rods that extend. A quinque is the one weapon the CCG trusts against a ghoul in full kagune.

entries.title: Ghoul ratings
entries.content: The CCG rates ghouls by danger, from low to high, with the ratings S, SS and SSS at the top. A rating rests on kill counts, the ghoul's kagune and the damage done in its last known case. An SSS rating means a ghoul the CCG believes can level a district, and it brings a full task force. Ratings are kept in files, and most people never see one.

entries.title: The Binge Eater
entries.content: The Binge Eater is the name the news gave to a ghoul who has killed across several nearby wards this year. Victims are found drained, with bite marks, and the CCG has not confirmed how many there are. The killings are moving closer to the 20th Ward one station at a time. Some officers think it is a single ghoul. Others think it is a crew copying the same method.

entries.title: The 11th Ward
entries.content: The 11th Ward is the dangerous ward next to yours: old warehouses, cheap hotels and sealed-off blocks where the CCG rarely goes without a squad. Ghouls there do not hide as carefully, and their crews trade in victims and information. A long road with a barrier at the station marks the border, and most people do not cross it after dark.

entries.title: Ward offices and district offices
entries.content: Tokyo is split into wards, each with a ward office for records and welfare and a CCG district office for ghouls. A district office keeps a file on every known ghoul in its ward and sends patrols on a schedule. Missing-person reports pass through the ward office first, so its welfare desk often hears of a disappearance before the police do.

entries.title: Ghoul masks
entries.content: A ghoul mask is a plain porcelain or resin face covering that some ghouls wear in public to hide the eyes and mouth when hunger or kagune starts to show. Masks are sold quietly in a few shops and are often made by hand. A mask in the street draws less notice than people expect, though a patrol that sees one will stop you.

entries.title: Ghoul crews
entries.content: Ghouls have no state. They live in small crews of a few people, bound by trust, debt and shared secrets. Crews trade information and food and settle quarrels with violence. Old ghouls like Yoshimura are respected, but many younger ghouls answer to no one, and crews break apart when a member is caught.

entries.title: Coexistence
entries.content: Some ghouls and some humans keep an unwritten peace. Ghouls do not feed inside the ward, humans do not hunt the ghouls who keep it, and both sides look away. It holds only while nobody breaks the rule. Anteiku is one of the places where the peace is kept, and the CCG has never officially recognized it.

entries.title: The old war
entries.content: Decades ago ghouls and humans fought open battles across the city, and the CCG grew out of those wars into a permanent force. Neither side won. People still argue over who started the killing, and families on both sides carry grudges. Schools teach the war as a warning.

world.vibe: Cold, close and watchful, with the real danger always one street away. People speak in favors and half-truths, and they say the ordinary thing while meaning the frightening one.

opening.note: Staged. Beat one: open on Anteiku before opening, the lane still and the CCG van across the way. Establish the closed sign, the coffee machine cooling, and the newspaper folded to the column about the body in the 17th Ward. Yoshimura speaks first, about the cold coming off the lane and the price of a cup, and only then, almost as an afterthought, asks whether you have eaten. Touka is at the back table with unopened notes and says nothing about the paper. Beat two: the interruption is the news and the phone. A radio on the shelf gives the Binge Eater's latest body, and someone has posted a photo of the campus board to the student group chat, and a link to the welfare office's missing-person page follows a minute later. Let each notification land without comment from anyone in the shop. Beat three: by the third turn the player is facing a real choice between going up to campus, where Amon's sweep is waiting at the gate, staying at Anteiku with Touka and the back room, or walking to the laundromat, where Chieko has heard something about the bus route that runs past the stations where the bodies were found. Do not let anyone explain the Binge Eater. Hold Professor Ueda's list and Emi Sakai's pulled files back until the player asks the right question, and let the silence in the shop stay honest.

cast.name: Yoshimura
cast.role: Owner of Anteiku, the coffee shop at the end of the lane in the 20th Ward. He has known most of the regulars on the block for decades and says about a tenth of what he knows to anyone who sits at the counter.
cast.look: Small and thin, white hair cut short, reading glasses on a cord, a grey cardigan over a pressed white shirt, spotted hands that stay perfectly steady when he pours.
cast.manner: Speaks slowly and kindly. Answers a hard question with the price of a cup of coffee, and ends a conversation by asking whether you have eaten today.
cast.secret: Yoshimura was once one of the most feared ghouls in the city, rated at the very top of the CCG's scale. He gave up killing decades ago and built Anteiku as a refuge. He quietly pays the rent of the Binge Eater's last victim's family.

cast.name: Touka Kirishima
cast.role: Part-time server at Anteiku and a second-year at a high school in the ward, who cuts class when it suits her. She is blunt with customers and never explains why she bothered saying anything at all.
cast.look: Tall and narrow in the shoulders, black hair cut to the jaw, a pale face with a sharp chin, a plain black apron over a grey work top, and a habit of standing with her weight on one hip.
cast.manner: Short sentences and dry humor. Sets cups down hard on the wood and refills water glasses without being asked, with her eyes on the door.
cast.secret: Touka is a ghoul who has lived on what Anteiku quietly supplies for two years. Lately she has started hearing the Binge Eater's name in her head as if it were a rival's, and she came within one street of going out alone last month.

cast.name: Nishiki Nishio
cast.role: A senior in pharmaceutical studies at Kamii who works the late shift at a pharmacy by the station. He talks to every shop owner in the 20th Ward as if he is personally responsible for them, and he treats the ward as his patch.
cast.look: Lean and tall, wavy brown hair pushed back, a grey sweater with the sleeves shoved up, a silver ring on his right thumb, and a laugh that carries across a room.
cast.manner: Quick and teasing. Recites drug names and dosages as if they were poetry, and corrects your pronunciation of street names to show he likes you.
cast.secret: Nishiki is a ghoul who has been taking the pharmacy's spare iron and blood-thinner stock to a small crew in the ward, so their RC readings stay low at the CCG blood checks. He has decided the Binge Eater is not his problem, because the 20th Ward is his.

cast.name: Koutarou Amon
cast.role: A First Class investigator with the Commission of Counter Ghoul, assigned to the campus sweep this month. He is polite to students, precise about paperwork and sincerely convinced that the law and the truth point the same way.
cast.look: Square in the shoulders, short hair parted sharp, a navy CCG jacket over a white shirt buttoned to the collar, a leather notebook always in his left hand, and steady grey eyes that rarely blink while he listens.
cast.manner: Formal and earnest. Speaks in complete sentences, never swears, keeps case numbers in his head like a prayer, and says for the victims when he means that he is certain.
cast.secret: Amon has the file on the Binge Eater's first victim, and the forensic report notes that the wounds were made by a quinque, not by a ghoul's teeth. He has not sent that note upward, because it points to a Commission weapon missing from its own armory.

cast.name: Hideyoshi Nagachika
cast.role: An economics student at Kamii who works weekend shifts at the bookshop by the station. He knows every rumor on campus within an hour of it starting and talks to everyone in the lecture hall whether they want it or not.
cast.look: Medium height, round face with a crooked smile, short dark hair that needs a cut, a denim jacket with a band pin on the lapel, and a phone that is always half out of his pocket.
cast.manner: Talks in quick bright bursts, types in lowercase, and sends memes to half the lecture hall at odd hours.
cast.secret: Hide is not a ghoul, but his older cousin was taken from a train platform in the 11th Ward last spring. He has been walking the 20th Ward's alleys at night, photographing the places the cousin might have been taken, convinced the Binge Eater leaves a pattern he can find.

cast.name: Tatsuya Ueda
cast.role: Professor of sociology at Kamii, who teaches a seminar on city life and has written three books about the 20th Ward's old neighborhoods. He has been quietly interviewing residents about who disappears and why, and the CCG has noticed.
cast.look: Stooped and grey-bearded, a crumpled tweed jacket with ink on the cuffs, half-moon glasses pushed up onto his forehead, and a battered leather satchel with a broken strap.
cast.manner: Digresses in long, friendly tangents. Cites sources by year, pushes his glasses up onto his forehead when he is about to say something he should not, and ends most sentences with as I was saying.
cast.secret: Ueda keeps a list of eleven people in the 20th Ward who vanished without explanation and all lived within a short walk of Anteiku. He suspects a feeding ring is running through the coffee shop's supplier, and he has not decided whether to publish it or to ask Yoshimura first.

cast.name: Chieko Hara
cast.role: Owns the laundromat on the side street behind Kamii Station and has known half the neighborhood for twenty years. She hears everything said over the dryers and gives away unclaimed socks to anyone who asks.
cast.look: Round-faced, short permed grey hair, a blue apron with a pen clipped to the pocket, reading glasses on a beaded chain, and sturdy forearms that fold a towel in one motion.
cast.manner: Hums enka under her breath, narrates the news as it plays, and changes the subject to food whenever someone says the word police.
cast.secret: Chieko's late husband was a ghoul killed in a CCG raid six years ago. She knows the smell of a ghoul on a customer's clothes, and for a year she has been washing one regular's bloodied jacket every Tuesday without telling anyone.

cast.name: Emi Sakai
cast.role: Caseworker at the 20th Ward Welfare Office. She takes missing-person reports from families and passes them to the police and sometimes to the Commission. She keeps the forms that never make the news.
cast.look: Neat and thin, dark hair tied back, a navy cardigan with a name badge clipped crooked, a stack of manila folders under one arm, and dark circles she has stopped trying to hide.
cast.manner: Speaks in short, flat sentences. Reads from forms word for word, never raises her voice, and gives the form number before she gives the answer.
cast.secret: Emi has noticed that the missing-person reports from the 20th Ward cluster along one bus route, and two cases were pulled from a police file by someone with CCG clearance. She has said nothing, because her own supervisor signed the pull order.

cast.name: Ken Kaneki
cast.role: A first-year literature student at Kamii who reads alone at Anteiku most afternoons. Quiet, polite and easy to overlook in a crowd. You have seen him on campus but never spoken more than a few words.
cast.look: Slim and pale, dark hair that falls over one eye, a grey cardigan over a white shirt, and a paperback always in hand or tucked under his arm.
cast.manner: Soft-spoken and apologetic. Touches the spine of whatever book he is holding when he is nervous. Answers a question with too many words and then goes quiet, as if he said more than he meant to. Bows slightly even to people his own age.
cast.secret: He went on a date with a woman named Rize Kamishiro two weeks ago and was badly hurt in an accident the same night. Since then he has not been able to eat, and the smell of food makes him sick. He has not told anyone.

systems.label: What you have seen
systems.meaning: How much of the ward's hidden life you have seen: a ghoul in the street, the back room at Anteiku, a body before the Commission reaches it. Low means an ordinary student. High means you know too much to look away.
systems.change: Rises when you watch a feeding, see a kagune, learn who is a ghoul or read a file you should not have. Falls slowly while you keep your routine and look the other way.

systems.label: Suspicion
systems.meaning: How much attention the Commission pays to you. Zero means no file. A hundred means a squad is at your door.
systems.change: Rises when you are seen near a known ghoul, when a sweep questions you, or when you file a report on the Binge Eater. Falls when you keep your routine and stay quiet.

systems.label: Ward Stability
systems.meaning: How calm the 20th Ward is, from zero, with killings on every street, to a hundred, with nothing unusual at all. Everyone in the ward shares it.
systems.change: Falls when a body turns up in the ward, when a CCG raid goes wrong in public, or when the Binge Eater moves in. Rises when the crews hold the peace and the Commission pulls back.

npcSystems.label: Trust
npcSystems.meaning: How much this person trusts you with what they know and what they keep.
npcSystems.change: Rises when you keep a confidence or show up when it matters. Falls when you lie to them or spread what they told you.

npcSystems.label: Need
npcSystems.meaning: How much this person needs something from you: a favor, a witness, a hand on a shift.
npcSystems.change: Rises when they are stuck or their trouble touches yours. Falls once you help them or refuse them plainly.

style.art: Dark urban Tokyo at night in muted grey and blue-black, with red accents: a red lantern over a shop door, a red coffee-shop sign, red warning tape, and one red light on a train platform.
style.avoid: Bright colors, cartoon monsters, gore close-ups and glossy stock-photo students.

heroes.name: Mei Ishikawa
heroes.description: A second-year from Saitama who commutes an hour each way and works the lunch rush at a gyudon counter on the main road.
heroes.look: Small and quick, black hair in a claw clip, a faded green hoodie, a canvas bag with a gyudon counter apron stuffed in it, and a habit of checking the exits in every room.
heroes.background: Grew up in a flat above her parents' noodle shop in Kawaguchi. Came to Tokyo on a scholarship with a stubborn plan to stay unnoticed. She has ridden past the station where the Binge Eater's first victim was found every weekday for a year.
heroes.carries: A commuter pass worn white at the corners, and a key ring from the noodle shop.

heroes.name: Ryota Hasegawa
heroes.description: A night-school law student who works the day desk at a business hotel by Kamii Station and never goes past the 11th Ward border after dark.
heroes.look: Broad-shouldered, a shaved head grown out to a shadow, a navy hotel jacket with one brass button missing, sneakers worn down at the heel, and a scar across the knuckles from a fight he will not describe.
heroes.background: Left a fishing town in Iwate when his family's business closed, and came to Tokyo to work. He shares a room above a pachinko parlor on the main road, where the noise covers almost everything. He wants a law degree and a small, quiet life.
heroes.carries: A thermos, a phone with a cracked screen, and a law textbook soft at the corners.

heroes.name: Jun Hayashi
heroes.description: An art student who draws the ward's alleys at night and sells the sketches at the Sunday market, always watching faces more than names.
heroes.look: Lean, shoulder-length hair dyed silver at the tips, a paint-stained canvas jacket, round wire glasses, and charcoal worked under the nails.
heroes.background: Grew up in Ota with a mother who runs a dry cleaner's and a father who never talked about his job. Left home for art school and fell for the old alleys of the 20th Ward. They have sketched a dozen corners that later became the places bodies were found.
heroes.carries: A roll of tracing paper and a set of pencils wrapped in a dish towel.
